name: Machir
overview: Machir was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, uniquely identified as the son of Manasseh (GEN 50:23). He is noted in Scripture as the progenitor of the Machirites (NUM 26:29), a significant clan within the tribe. His lineage highlights his role in the genealogical and tribal structure of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Machir is a proper name meaning 'bought,' as recorded in Genesis 50:23. This meaning is given without indication that the name was divinely assigned, reflecting a common Hebrew personal name rather than a title or divine epithet.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Machir as the son of Manasseh (GEN 50:23) and the father of Gilead (NUM 26:29). Other inferred relationships include being the father of Abijah (1CH 2:21) and possibly connected as husband to Maacah and Zelophehad, as well as father to Peresh and Sheresh (1CH 7:15-16), though these latter connections are less certain.
scriptureSignificance: Machir's significance lies in his place within the tribe of Manasseh and as the ancestor of the Machirites, a notable clan mentioned in the wilderness census. His lineage contributes to the unfolding history of Israel's tribal divisions and inheritance patterns, emphasizing God's providential preservation and organization of His people through genealogical lines.
